# Layouts and Slots

`+layout.ets` files wrap pages. A page's layouts are every `+layout` from its own folder up to `pb_pages/`, applied innermost first. A folder may have one layout, written as `+layout.ets` (or `+layout.tsx`, see [TSX](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx)). A layout can't be Markdown: `+layout.md` is an error at startup.

```plaintext
pb_pages/
  +layout.ets          # applied last (outermost)
  products/
    +layout.ets        # applied first
    [id].ets
```

For `/products/123`, `[id].ets` renders, then `products/+layout.ets` wraps it, then `+layout.ets` wraps that.

## `slot()`

In a layout, `slot()` returns the content being wrapped: the page, or the inner layout.

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/+layout.ets -->
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <title>My Application</title>
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <%- slot() %>
  </main>
  <footer>&copy; <%= new Date().getFullYear() %> My Application</footer>
</body>
</html>
```

`<%- slot %>` without parentheses prints the same content, so 0.x layouts that wrote it still work.

## Named slots

A page (or an inner layout) defines a named slot with `slot(name, fn)`. `fn`'s output is captured and nothing is output in place. A layout reads it with `slot(name)`, which returns `''` if it isn't defined.

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/products/[id].ets -->
<% slot('title', () => { %><%= data.product.getString('name') %><% }) %>
<h1><%= data.product.getString('name') %></h1>
```

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/+layout.ets -->
<html>
  <head><title><%- slot('title') || 'My shop' %></title></head>
  <body><%- slot() %></body>
</html>
```

- Named slots defined by the page or by any inner layout are visible to every outer layout.
- Defining the same name again replaces it. Inside the new definition's `fn`, `slot(name)` still returns the previous content, so a layout can wrap it:

```ets
<!-- pb_pages/docs/+layout.ets -->
<% slot('title', () => { %>Docs: <%- slot('title') %><% }) %>
<main><%- slot() %></main>
```

## Data in layouts

Layouts render after the page, with the same `ctx`. Everything middleware, the page's code and the page put on `ctx.data` or `ctx.meta` is there.

## When layouts are skipped

- When the response isn't HTML (a handler set another `Content-Type`).
- When a handler or middleware sent the response itself (`ctx.res.json`, `ctx.res.html`, `ctx.res.redirect`, ...).
- For [endpoints](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes), which have no template.
- After `ctx.res.layout(false)`, called from middleware, the page's code or the page itself.
- With the [Datastar add-on](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar), for requests that carry `Datastar-Request: true`.

To serve HTML fragments without the site layout, call `ctx.res.layout(false)`, put the layout in a group (`(site)/+layout.ets`) and the fragments outside it, or send them with `ctx.res.html()`.
